chunks: And from him (Al-Ukhu) from Al-Abid from Al-Fadl ibn Al-Mubarak Al-Basri from his father from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, a man is obligated to free a believing slave-girl but he cannot find one; what should he do?' He said, 'You are commanded to free young children (from slavery); if one turns out to be a believer, that suffices, and if not, there is no blame upon you.'

key_terms.خَرَجَتْ: Turned out to be / was found to be

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for freeing a believing slave-girl when one cannot find an adult?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a practical solution for *kaffarah* (expiation) when a specific adult slave is unavailable, directing the individual to free young children (*al-atfal*) who are in a state of *fitrah* (innate potential for faith). This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle of presuming the default state of children to be neutral or potentially believing, thereby allowing the expiation to be fulfilled conditionally; if the child later embraces Islam, the obligation is discharged, ensuring the debtor is not burdened indefinitely. This mechanism reflects the mercy and flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding financial and spiritual obligations.
